events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: NDMUNC III Day Three
events.summary: NDMUNC III is an immersive dive into global leadership, diplomacy, and academic excellence. Staffed entirely by undergraduate students at the University of Notre Dame, we at NDMUNC pride ourselves on providing students with a holistic experience in global policy. Delegates participate in substantive committee sessions that emphasize thorough research, structured debate, and strategic negotiation. Through thoughtfully designed committees and dynamic crisis simulations, students will learn to confront complex international issues and are expected to draft innovative solutions. This is a registered Model UN conference, not an open drop-in mixer; consult the host about delegation or staffing eligibility.

events.title: 12th Annual Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering Graduate Research Symposium
events.summary: ND Energy is pleased to be a sponsor of the 12th Annual Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering Graduate Research Symposium on Saturday, October 3, from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. in the Dahnke Ballroom at the University of Notre Dame. This year's symposium will showcase a wide range of research and disciplines focused on the theme of Beyond Acceleration: Engineering Lasting Solutions in a Rapidly Advancing World. With a diverse audience comprised of peers, faculty, alumni, and industry partners, as well as invited speakers, participants will learn about the latest technologies, breakthroughs, and other scholarly achievements in the following key research areas: Energy and Sustainability Nano- and Micro-Fluidics Simulation and Theory Systems Engineering Materials Science Nanotechnology Bioengineering Watch for the symposium schedule and other details coming soon on the symposium website here. Originally published at energy.nd.edu.

events.title: "Now You See It": Ekphrastic Poetry Workshop with Alexandra Lytton Regalado and Emma Trelles
events.summary: Alexandra Lytton Regalado and Emma Trelles Poetry in conversation with visual art is called ekphrasis. As poet Edward Hirsch has noted, ekphrastic writing “braves the mystery dividing the seen from the unseen,” and teaches us “to look and look again more closely.” In this creative writing workshop, you’ll practice looking and writing more deeply through the lens of color in abstract and figurative works. We’ll approach the art of the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art as portals into memories, experience, and imagination. We’ll also offer you a booklet that includes sample poems and the images that sparked them, as well as prompts to get you started. We’ll share how ekphrasis can unfold into an opportunity to create community and artistic magic. At the end of this workshop, we will collaborate on a poem, with everyone invited (though not required!) to share their work or questions about the writing process and the connection between visual art and poetry, also known as the sister arts. Alexandra Lytton Regalado is a Salvadoran-American author, translator, and editor. She is the author of Re […] hip from the California Arts Council and a Poet Laureate Fellowship from the Academy of American Poets. A graduate CantoMundo Fellow, her translations were longlisted in the Best Literary Translations 2027 anthology, and her work recently appears in Poetry International; New England Review; Poetry; and the Academy’s Poem-A-Day series. She is series editor of the Alta California Chapbook Prize, open to Latine poets in the U.S. and published in bilingual editions by Gunpowder Press. emmatrelles.com Hirsch, Edward, ed. Transforming Vision: Writers on Art, Chicago: Art Institute of Chicago, 1994. Originally published at raclinmurphymuseum.nd.edu. This is an excerpt of a longer announcement. Consult the original listing for full program, registration, and attendance requirements.

events.title: The Met Opera Live in HD: "Così fan tutte" (Mozart)
events.summary: The Met Opera Live in HD237 minutes (One intermission) LiveThe Met: Live in HD season kicks off with Mozart's satirical comedy of fickle young love, one of the composer's most sublime creations. Phelim McDermott's "colorful, inventive" (The New York Times) staging, inspired by Coney Island in the 1950s, sets the uproarious story at a boardwalk amusement park, where the two pairs of lovers at the heart of the tale find themselves on one emotional—and literal—thrill ride after another. Soprano Federica Lombardi and mezzo-soprano Samantha Hankey sing Fiordiligi and Dorabella, opposite tenor Duke Kim and baritone Andrey Zhilikhovsky as Ferrando and Guglielmo. Bass-baritone Gerald Finley reprises his portrayal of the cynical Don Alfonso, with soprano Ana María Martínez as the witty maid Despina. GET TICKETS *Sponsored by the Jill A. Fischer Endowment for Excellence in Live Opera Broadcasts.

events.title: Film: "The Flowers of St. Francis" (1950)
events.summary: Classics at the BrowningDirected by Roberto RosselliniWith Brother Nazario Gerardi, Brother Severino Pisacane, Aldo FabriziNot Rated, 87 minutesIn Italian with English subtitlesIn advance of the Feast of St. Francis and the 800th anniversary of his death, we are exploring a classic cinematic representation of his life. In a series of simple and joyous vignettes, director Roberto Rossellini and co-writer Federico Fellini lovingly convey the universal teachings of the People's Saint: humility, compassion, faith, and sacrifice. Gorgeously photographed to evoke the medieval paintings of Saint Francis's time, and cast with monks from the Nocera Inferiore Monastery, The Flowers of St. Francis is a timeless and moving portrait of the search for spiritual enlightenment. RESERVE TICKETS This is a free but ticketed event. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: Catholic Leadership, Integral Ecology, and the Call of Laudato Si’
events.summary: In an era of accelerating climate change, widening inequality and geopolitical uncertainty, how are Catholic institutions called to respond to the world’s most pressing challenges? Join Cardinal Peter Turkson and Mary Gallagher, the Marilyn Keough Dean of the Keough School of Global Affairs, for a conversation on Catholic Leadership, integral human development and the role of faith, scholarship and research in advancing justice and peace. Their discussion will explore the enduring call of Laudato Si’, the interconnected challenges facing our world and the opportunities for Catholic institutions to advance knowledge and action for the common good. This event is in partnership with the Keough School’s Ansari Institute for Global Engagement With Religion. About Cardinal Peter Turkson Cardinal Peter Kodwo Appiah Turkson, chancellor of the Pontifical Academies of Social Sciences and Sciences, was a key figure in the drafting of Pope Francis’ 2015 encyclical, Laudato Si’ and is a leading voice on Catholic social teaching, justice and integral human development. events.title: Nuclear Physics Seminar: Dr. Melina Avila Coronado, Argonne National Laboratory
events.summary: Reactions in X-Ray Bursts: New Constraints from Direct Measurements Dr. Melina Avila CoronadoAssistant Physicist-ExperimentalistArgonne National Laboratory Type I X-ray bursts provide a unique environment for explosive nucleosynthesis driven by sequences of proton captures, a-induced reactions, and b-decays on proton-rich nuclei. The competition among these processes governs the breakout from the hot CNO cycles, the subsequent reaction flow along the rp- and ap-processes, and ultimately the burst light curve and energy generation. Reliable modeling of these events therefore depends on accurate nuclear reaction rates over a wide range of unstable nuclei. Many of the most important reactions in X-ray bursts remain poorly constrained experimentally. Direct measurements at astrophysical energies are often hindered by small cross sections and limited radioactive beam intensities. Recent advances in radioactive ion beam facilities and experimental techniques have created new opportunities to overcome these challenges, enabling direct measurements of astrophysically important reactions. In this presentation, I will highlight recent experimental progress on reactions relevant to X-ray bursts using the active-target detector MUSIC. Hosted by Prof. Bardayan

events.summary: In celebration of the international Big Draw Festival, drawing materials will be available to satisfy your creative itch all October long. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.

events.title: Model Theory Seminar: Atticus Stonestrom - University of Notre Dame
events.summary: Speaker: Atticus StonestromUniversity of Notre DameWill give a Model Theory Seminar entitled:New results for NIP groups, part 2Abstract: Let T be a first-order theory and G a definable group of T, and assume for convenience that T has constant symbols naming a model M_0. A definable subset of G is said to be `strong f-generic' if no left translate of it forks over M_0; a fundamental result in the structure theory of NIP groups, due to Hrushovski and Pillay, is that, if T is NIP, then G is definably amenable if and only if the non strong f-generic subsets of G form an ideal. (Meanwhile, by a much earlier result of Pillay, if T is simple then the non strong f-generic subsets of G always form an ideal.) Strong f-generic types play an indispensable role in the study of definably amenable NIP groups. I will present a new notion which I hope to serve as a substitute for strong f-generic sets in the study of arbitrary (ie not definably amenable) NIP groups. Namely, let us call a definable subset of G ‘piecewise strong f-generic’ if some union of finitely many left translates of it is strong f-generic. The main theorem I will present is that, if T is NIP, then the non piecewise strong f-generic subsets of G form an ideal. As a quick consequence I will give a new and improved proof of Gismatullin's result on the ‘existence’ of G000, and next week in the Part II talk I will present two other applications.Date: 10-06-2026Time: 10:30 amLocation: 125 Hayes Healy Center Download Poster [PDF, 157k]

events.title: Astrophysics Seminar: Saloni Deekpak, University of Notre Dame
events.summary: The Metal Enrichment History of the CGM and IGM Across ~12 Gyr: The BRIDGE Survey Saloni DeepakDepartment of Physics and AstronomyUniversity of Notre Dame The growth and evolution of galaxies are regulated by their exchange of gas with the circumgalactic and intergalactic medium (CGM/IGM). These multiphase reservoirs supply the fuel for star formation and carry the imprint of stellar and AGN feedback, so their metal content constrains feedback and accretion in cosmological simulations, the enrichment timescales of different gas phases, and the cosmic baryon cycle. Metallicity surveys of H I-selected absorbers exist at z < 1 and z > 2.2, but at Cosmic Noon (1 <= z <= 2.2), the peak epoch of star formation and AGN activity, the cool CGM and IGM traced by absorbers with log N_HI < 20.3 remain largely unconstrained. I will present BRIDGE, a survey that fills this gap by combining archival HST UV spectra with Keck/HIRES and VLT/UVES optical spectra. From BRIDGE-I, I report metallicities, densities, and ionization conditions for 105 absorbers with 16.4 ≤ log N_HI < 20.3, whose column densities at Cosmic Noon correspond to overdensities typical of the CGM. Comparing with lower and higher redshifts, I find that lower-overdensity CGM gas has already reached its z < 1 metallicity by Cosmic Noon, while higher-overdensity gas continues to be enriched at later times, with no absorber below [X/H] ~ -2 in the densest gas. I will show that metallicity correlates with overdensity, consistent with metals tracing the large-scale collapse of baryons. I will then turn to a complementary study of a lensed quasar pair whose sightlines intersect three Cosmic Noon absorbers, resolving metallicity and density variations on kpc scales within individual CGM structures. This work shows that metals are poorly mixed within individual CGM structures on kpc scales, and demonstrates the power of lensed sightlines for resolving that patchiness directly.

events.title: Particle Physics Seminar: Will Wolf, University of Oxford
events.summary: Scalar Field Dark Energy in Light of DESI Will WolfGraduate StudentUniversity of Oxford I present an assessment of the current observational status of single scalar field models of dark energy. Motivated by recent cosmological measurements -- including baryon acoustic oscillations, Type Ia supernovae, and CMB data -- I examine both the evidence from this data that appears to be hinting at dynamical evolution in the dark energy equation of state and whether a scalar field offers a viable explanation for the accelerated expansion of the Universe. Working within an effective field theory (EFT) framework, I argue that cosmological observations are fundamentally limited and can at most constrain a small number of parameters that govern scalar field dynamics. I argue that quintessence remains only marginally distinguishable from a cosmological constant, Λ, and that more general EFT extensions exhibit modest statistical preference, though such evidence is sensitive to data set selection and prior assumptions. These extended models generically predict fifth forces and modifications to the gr […] ely in agreement and do not yet offer strong discriminatory power between most scalar field constructs, while screening mechanisms remain theoretically non-trivial and difficult to assess observationally. Looking ahead to Stage IV surveys we forecast improvements in constraints on the dark energy behaviour; although there will be some tightening of bounds, I argue that the problem of underdetermination will persist. I conclude that while single scalar field dark energy remains a natural and flexible framework, its ultimate viability will hinge on improved low-redshift growth measurements and a clearer understanding of gravitational screening. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: Lynch Lecture: The Yamabe Problem
events.summary: Andrea Malchiodi, Ph.D.Professor of MathematicsScuola Normale SuperioreFlorence, Italy The Yamabe problem is an extension to manifolds of dimension greater or equal to three of the classical Uniformization question for Riemann surfaces. Formulated in 1960, it serves as a paradigm for geometric partial differential equations exhibiting a lack of compactness. Although the existence of solutions was fully settled in the 1980s through the landmark contributions of Trudinger, Aubin and Schoen, the problem has recently revealed new and surprising aspects. In this talk, we will discuss the foundational results in the literature, alongside current perspectives and open problems.

Held will speak on the question: "Do Jews and Christians Love the Same Way?" Originally published at theology.nd.edu.

events.title: The Solar Revolution: How Photovoltaics are Rewriting the Rules of our Energy System
events.summary: Danielle Merfeld, Global Chief Technology Officer at Qcells, will outline how solar energy is no longer just an alternative energy source but is transitioning into a cornerstone of national security and economic independence. Advances in solar PV technology and domestic manufacturing, combined with the rapid integration of energy storage, are enabling a resilient, decarbonized grid for the next generation. She will also explore how the frontiers of PV innovation are stretching into outer space to power massive satellite constellations and enable permanent lunar installations. Danielle Merfeld Bio Danielle serves as Global Chief Technology Officer at Qcells, leading research and development for advanced solar products, power electronics, system controls, and energy software. In this role, she drives efforts to build the first fully integrated solar supply chain in the United States. She previously directed technical strategy at GE Renewable Energy across wind, solar, hydro, and grid solutions, where she also established GE's first business-wide sustainability initiative to reduce Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions. Elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 2021, Danielle holds a B.S. from the University of Notre Dame and a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from Northwestern University. She serves on Notre Dame's Board of Trustees and advises several national energy bodies, including Georgia Tech's Strategic Energy Institute. Originally published at energy.nd.edu.

Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: Lecture—"Jacques Maritain in Africa: Catholic Social Thinking and African Political Thought"
events.summary: Abstract: This talk will look at how Jacques Maritain's life and thought influenced Léopold Senghor and Julius Nyerere—two of the three most important African political thinkers of the twentieth century—in order to explore how concepts Maritain wrote about, such as personalism, integral humanism, and the genuine political notion of the state, influenced African postcolonial thought, particularly the phenomenon of African Socialism. More broadly we will examine how mid-century Catholic ideas impacted African and global audiences. Speaker Bio: Ethan Sanders is a 2026–27 Maritain Research Grant awardee and chair and professor of history at Regis University in Denver, Colorado. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Cambridge in global intellectual history with a focus on Africa. His first book, Building the African Nation (Cambridge, 2025), explored the growth of "African" identity and pan-Africanism in East Africa, and his second book project, Julius Nyerere: Africa's Global Visionary of the Twentieth Century (under contract with Yale) is a religious and intellectual biography of Julius Nyerere through a global lens. The event is cosponsored by the Maritain Center and the Global Catholic Research Initiative. Originally published at maritain.nd.edu.

events.title: Film: "Mirror" (1975)
events.summary: MFA Students Pick Some Films for Us to WatchDirected by Arseniy TarkovskiyWith Margarita Terekhova, Filipp Yankovskiy, Ignat DaniltsevNot Rated, 107 minutes, DCPIn Russian and Spanish with English subtitlesIntroductory reading by Tim Morrison.A senses-ravishing odyssey through the halls of time and memory, Andrei Tarkovsky's sublime reflection on 20th century Russian history is as much a film as it is a poem composed in images, as much a work of cinema as it is a hypnagogic hallucination. In a richly textured collage of varying film stocks and newsreel footage, the recollections of a dying poet flash before our eyes, dreams mingling with scenes of childhood, wartime, and marriage, all imbued with the mystic power of a trance. Largely dismissed by Soviet critics upon its release due to its elusive narrative structure, Mirror has since taken its place as one of the titan director's most renowned and influential works, a stunning personal statement from an artist transmitting his innermost thoughts and feelings directly from psyche to screen. GET TICKETS Copresented by the Creative Writing Program and the Meg and John P. Brogan Endowment for Classic Cinema.

events.title: Crash Course series: "Fighting Poverty with Economics"
events.summary: Get a one-hour sampling of the power of a Notre Dame liberal arts education with the College of Arts & Letters' Crash Course series on home football Fridays. Each event features an A&L professor leading a class session pulled directly from some of the most popular and riveting courses on campus. "Fighting Poverty with Economics" with Adrienne Judson(Economics) What is poverty? How has poverty changed over time? How can we learn what works and what doesn’t when alleviating poverty? In this session, attendees will explore these questions through the lens of economics, combining theory and empirical evidence. They'll also be introduced to the Poverty Research Fellows, an innovative program that engages A&L students in the fight against poverty, preparing them to join the next generation of anti-poverty researchers, policymakers, and leaders. Alumni, friends, prospective students and their parents, and anyone else on campus are welcome. Visit Crash Course for a complete listing of courses this season. Originally published at al.nd.edu.

events.title: Book Launch: "The Irish Pope: Paul Cullen, 1803-1878"
events.summary: Please join the Keough-Naughton Institute, the Global Catholic Research Initiative, and the Department of History as they celebrate the publication of Professor Colin Barr's new book, The Irish Pope: Paul Cullen, 1803-1878 (Cambridge University Press, 2026). Barr will be joined in conversation with Thomas Bartlett, professor emeritus of Irish history at the University of Aberdeen. Copies of the book will be available for purchase after the event. About The Irish Pope Paul Cullen was without question the most important Irishman of his generation and a figure of global importance. He is also among the least understood. Examining every aspect of Cullen's life and career, Colin Barr explores how Cullen was characterised by his contemporaries as an 'Italian monk', 'the deadly foe of Irish liberty', 'an obscurantist run mad', or 'the most malignant enemy of the English & English Government in Ireland.' One frustrated contemporary called him 'the Pope of Ireland'. This study explores Cullen's early years and education in papal Rome, his career in the curia and then in Ireland, as Archbishop […] aking World, 1829-1914 (Cambridge University Press, 2020), The European Culture Wars in Ireland: The Callan Schools Affair, 1868-1881 (University College Dublin Press, 2010), Paul Cullen, John Henry Newman, and the Catholic University of Ireland, 1845-65 (University of Notre Dame Press, 2003), Nation/Nazione: Irish Nationalism and the Italian Risorgimento (co-edited with Michele Finelli and Anne O’Connor; University College Dublin Press, 2014), and Religion and Greater Ireland: Christianity and Irish Global Networks, 1750-1950 (co-edited with Hilary M. Carey; McGill-Queen’s University Press, 2015). Originally published at irishstudies.nd.edu. This is an excerpt of a longer announcement. events.title: Film: "The Exorcist" Double Feature
events.summary: Classics in the BrowningCome for one or both films. A 15-minute intermission will occur between the screenings.The Exorcist (1973)Directed by William FriedkinWith Linda Blair, Ellen Burstyn, Max von SydowRated R, 122 minutes, DCPIn English, Latin, Greek, French, German, Arabic, and Kurdish with English subtitlesExorcist II: The Heretic (1977)Directed by John BoormanWith Linda Blair, Richard Burton, Louise FletcherIn English, French, Spanish, and Latin with English subtitlesThe impact of The Exorcist on horror films, American Catholicism, and children's (and parents') dreams is difficult to understate. When released in 1973, the film broke industrial and critical bounds becoming the first horror film to be nominated for the Best Picture Oscar. Further, its ability to work the profane into a "sacred" film became a blueprint many have copied — and continue to do so. When Exorcist II: The Heretic hit in 1977, it was almost immediately labeled the opposite; it was, itself, heretical to the vision of the first by, according to the New York Times, being laughable and "cold mashed potatoes." Recently, though, that same newspaper ran a piece on how John Boorman's sequel deserves more respect, and indeed it has the love of Martin Scorsese (who prefers the sequel to the original) and Pauline Kael delighted in Exorcist II's "visionary crazy grandeur." As we start October, come check out both to see which possesses you more. GET TICKETS Co-presented by the Department of American Studies.

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: "Drawing from the Well": An Irish Traditional Music Concert
events.summary: Drawing from the Well: Irish Traditional Music Concert2:30 to 4 p.m. (Doors at 2 p.m.)Patricia George Decio Theatre, DeBartolo Performing Arts Center$25 General AdmissionLog in for special Notre Dame student, staff, and faculty pricing.$15 Faculty and StaffFree for Students Reserve Your Tickets The acclaimed Drawing from the Well concert series, curated by the Irish Traditional Music Archive (Dublin, Ireland), is coming back to the US, this time to the University of Notre Dame, home of the famed Chief O’Neill Collection, often referred to simply as “the book” or “the bible” of Irish traditional music, preserved in the Hesburgh Library’s Rare Books & Special Collections. Drawing from the Well: Notre Dame is sponsored by Notre Dame Dublin and the Keough-Naughton Institute for Irish Studies. ITMA’s US projects are co-funded by the Government of Ireland’s Department of Culture, Communications & Sport and Department of Foreign Affairs & Trade as a part of America250. The Drawing from the Well concert program platforms leading Irish traditional musicians, singers and dancers, with performa […] sts will engage with those archival treasures to inspire a unique performance. Ireland’s Department of Foreign Affairs & Trade and Department of Culture, Communications & Sport has partnered with ITMA to support US concerts, satellite cultural events, and larger research projects in celebration of America250, highlighting Ireland’s deep historical, cultural, and familial links with the United States. The result of this work culminates in the creation of a digital map highlighting Irish music, song and dance in all 50 US states, which will be launched at the Notre Dame Drawing from the Well concert. events.title: Concert: Trio Caspar
events.summary: Presenting Series Trio Caspar is an innovative union of three individual voices, and the first group named the Colburn Conservatory inaugural Honors Chamber Music Ensemble. Founded in 2024 by clarinetist Andrea Caputo, violinist Jason Moon, and pianist Bogang Hwang, Trio Caspar aims to bring a fresh perspective of the highest standard to less frequently performed chamber works. The trio was awarded the Gold Medal, Lift Every Voice Prize, and Horszowski Trio Prize for Piano Ensemble at the 2026 Fischoff Competition in the Senior String Division, as well as the Audience Award and 2nd Prize at the 2026 Yellow Springs Chamber Music Competition.The name pays homage to the German painter Caspar David Friedrich, whose exploration of the complexity of individualism inspires the ensemble's distinctive sound. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: EHUM Speaker: Thea Riofrancos
events.summary: Biography Professor of Political Science at Providence College, a Strategic Co-Director of the Climate and Community Institute, and a fellow at the Transnational Institute.Extraction: The Frontiers of Green Capitalism Will green capitalism save us from the climate crisis? "Clean" technologies and renewable energy are certainly growing sites of capitalist investment, with government policies playing a key role in making these sectors profitable. But the supply chains that produce the technologies pose vexing dilemmas for the energy transition. These dilemmas are most dramatic at the extractive frontiers of green capitalism: where the natural resources needed to manufacture electric vehicles and build windmills are extracted. In this talk, we will unpack these challenges through the lens of lithium, a so-called "critical mineral" essential for its role in decarbonizing one of the most polluting sectors: transportation. With forecasters predicting an enormous surge in lithium demand, exceeding existing supplies, Global North governments and downstream firms scramble to "secure" lithium, resulting in a new state-corporate alliance and the return of vertical integration. Meanwhile, Global South governments are attempting to leverage critical mineral deposits into sustainable and sovereign economic development. And, across the world, environmental and Indigenous movements contest the rapid expansion of extraction, defending ecosystems, livelihoods, and waterways already under pressure from global warming from a new boom in mining. It is in the play of these forces, unfolding amidst geopolitical rivalry and economic turbulence, that the energy transition will be forged. To conclude, we will explore the possibility of a less mining-intensive pathway to zero carbon transportation. Originally published at reilly.nd.edu.

events.title: Celebrating the Big Draw Festival: Make Your Mark
events.summary: In celebration of the international Big Draw Festival, drawing materials will be available to satisfy your creative itch all October long. Head to the Learning Commons to pick up supplies (or bring your own–solid graphite only, please) and then into the galleries to sketch one of your favorite works of art. Take your drawing with you or add it to the display wall to share with others. Parking is available in the Visitor Lot immediately north of the Sculpture Park for a fee during the week (before 4:30 p.m.). Free two-hour parking is available in the Eddy Street Commons Parking Garage or along Angela Blvd. After 4:30 p.m. and on weekends, parking is free and available in any non-gated campus lot. If traveling via South Bend Transpo, take the No.7 bus and use the Eddy St. Commons stop. About the Big Draw Festival The Big Draw Festival is a worldwide celebration of drawing, bringing people together through the power of creativity. The Festival provides a platform to explore drawing and mark-making in all its forms. Since its launch in 2000, The Big Draw has championed the universal language of drawing as a tool for learning, expression, and innovation. By taking part, you join a global movement that promotes creativity, wellbeing, and arts education. Originally published at raclinmurphymuseum.nd.edu.

events.title: EFD Seminar Series: A Flood Early Warning System (FEWS) to Predict Critical Floods in the TX Hill Country
events.summary: Bio: Dr. Philip B. Bedient Herman Brown Professor of Engineering in the Dept of Civil and Environmental Eng at Rice University. He teaches and performs research in surface water hydrology, coastal defense, disaster management, and flood modeling and prediction systems. He has directed 130 research projects over the past 50 years, has written over 220 articles in journals and conference proceedings. He is lead author on a textbook on “Hydrology and Floodplain Analysis” (Pearson, 6th ed., 2018) used in over 60 universities across the Unites States. Dr. Bedient received the Herman Brown Endowed Chair of Engineering in 2002 at Rice University, and received Fellow ASCE in 2006. He received the C.V. Theis Award from the American Institute of Hydrology in 2007 and the prestigious Ray K. Linsley Award in honor of outstanding contributions in 2007 for surface water hydrology. Dr. Bedient has five decades of experience working on flood and flood prediction problems in the U.S. He routinely runs computer models such as HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, ADCIRC, and others for advanced hydrologic analysis, flood […] ve 2-3 hours of lead time on rainfall events. While flood warnings are often associated with sirens or text alerts, the new system begins much earlier—using radar-derived rainfall data fed into advanced hydrologic and hydraulic models to forecast flood water depths at specific locations. The system uses a floodplain map library of over 100 maps created by rainfalls from 3 to 15 inches per day, and radar rainfall each 15 min is used to select the appropriate inundation map. The FEWS will be able to provide 1-2 hours of advanced warning of a flood for sheltering of evacuation to higher ground. Originally published at environmentalchange.nd.edu. events.title: "The Science of How the Arts Save Lives": A Talk with Daisy Fancourt
events.summary: Join the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art for an evening with Daisy Fancourt, researcher, professor at University College London, and author of Art Cure: The Science of How the Arts Save Lives, which is a Sunday Times Bestseller and a shortlisted title for the Women's Prize for non-fiction. An internationally recognized leader in the growing field of arts and health, Fancourt studies how music, visual art, dance, theater, and museum engagement can reduce stress, improve well-being, strengthen social connections, and support healing. During this talk, Fancourt will explore the powerful role the arts can play in human flourishing, offering new perspectives on why creative experiences matter and how art museums are not only places to encounter art, but spaces where wellness, reflection, and human connection can thrive. Parking is available in the Visitor Lot immediately behind the museum, north of the Sculpture Park, for free after 4:30 p.m. and on weekends. Parking can also be found along Angela Blvd. If traveling via South Bend Transpo, take the No.7 bus and use the stop at Notre Dame Ave. and Angela Blvd. Originally published at raclinmurphymuseum.nd.edu.

events.summary: Presenting Series To mark the 250th anniversary of America, American Dialogues celebrates the nation's ever-evolving story through newly commissioned works and reimagined classics that give voice to our shared ideals and diverse perspectives. Highlights include Rachel McFarlane's new title work as well as Maurice Ravel's timeless "Blues" movement from the Violin Sonata. Works by Roberto Sierra and Jessie Montgomery offer vibrant explorations of heritage and transformation. At the same time, Stravinsky's Concerto for Strings in D connects past and present in a timeless meditation on artistic freedom.Through music that bridges time and culture, American Dialogues invites audiences to engage in a musical conversation about who we are—and who we aspire to become.Sphinx Virtuosi is a dynamic, self-conducted chamber orchestra and the flagship performing ensemble of the Sphinx Organization, the nation's leading nonprofit dedicated to transforming the arts. Comprising 18 of the nation's most accomplished professional string players, Sphinx Virtuosi is redefining classical music through artistic excellence, pioneering programming, and cultural leadership. Recognized for their artistry and commanding presence, Sphinx Virtuosi has been praised by The New York Times as "top-notch, more essential at this moment than ever." The Strad praises their "elegant ascent into the upper ranks of string orchestras," a testament to their growing influence in the field.Grammy winning mezzo-soprano J'Nai Bridges, is known for her "plush-voiced mezzo-soprano" (The New York Times), and "calmly commanding stage presence" (The New Yorker) has been "marked out at an early stage as a singer headed for top flight" (Financial Times), gracing the world's leading operatic and concert stages "with a voice both voluptuous and statuesque" (The New York Times). Bridges is a recipient of the prestigious 2018 Sphinx Medal of Excellence Award. GET TICKETS *Recommended for ages five and up.

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.

events.title: Algebraic Geometry and Commutative Algebra Seminar: Shuddhodan Kadattur Vasudevan - University of Michigan
events.summary: Speaker: Shuddhodan Kadattur VasudevanUniversity of Notre DameWill give a Algebraic Geometry and Commutative Algebra Seminar entitled:Vanishing in the limitAbstract: An affine variety of dimension $d$ has no mod $\ell$ cohomology above degree $d$, whereas a projective variety of positive dimension has cohomology in degree $2d$ (the class of a point!). In characteristic zero, Scholze showed that for subvarieties of projective space the cohomology above the dimension vanishes in the limit along the “mock Frobenius” tower, and Esnault proved this in every characteristic different from $\ell$. Bhatt-Schnell-Scholze asked whether the same holds for subvarieties of an abelian variety $A$ in characteristic $p eq\ell$, along the tower of multiplication by $\ell$. We prove that it does. events.summary: The Met Opera Live in HD209 minutes (one intermission) LiveTwo of opera's most extraordinary artists return to The Met: Live in HD for Verdi's thrilling take on the immortal Shakespearean tale of the scheming couple determined to seize power at any cost. Following past triumphs in many of Verdi's signature baritone roles, Quinn Kelsey is the Scottish king haunted by the ghosts of his murderous ascent to the throne, opposite Lise Davidsen—the world's reigning dramatic soprano—as the power-mad Lady Macbeth, whose ruinous ambition damns them both. Met Music Director Yannick Nézet-Séguin takes the podium for a penetrating production by Louisa Proske, a brilliant young director making waves around the world. Fischer Endowment for Excellence in Live Opera Broadcasts.

events.title: Celebrating the Big Draw Festival: Make Your Mark
events.summary: In celebration of the international Big Draw Festival, drawing materials will be available to satisfy your creative itch all October long. Head to the Learning Commons to pick up supplies (or bring your own–solid graphite only, please) and then into the galleries to sketch one of your favorite works of art. Take your drawing with you or add it to the display wall to share with others. Parking is available in the Visitor Lot immediately north of the Sculpture Park for a fee during the week (before 4:30 p.m.). Free two-hour parking is available in the Eddy Street Commons Parking Garage or along Angela Blvd. After 4:30 p.m. and on weekends, parking is free and available in any non-gated campus lot. If traveling via South Bend Transpo, take the No.7 bus and use the Eddy St. Commons stop. About the Big Draw Festival The Big Draw Festival is a worldwide celebration of drawing, bringing people together through the power of creativity. The Festival provides a platform to explore drawing and mark-making in all its forms. Since its launch in 2000, The Big Draw has championed the universal language of drawing as a tool for learning, expression, and innovation. By taking part, you join a global movement that promotes creativity, wellbeing, and arts education. Originally published at raclinmurphymuseum.nd.edu.

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.

events.title: Nuclear Physics Seminar: Dr. John Wilkinson, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory
events.summary: AMS & Nuclear Data at the Center for Accelerator Mass Spectrometry (CAMS) Dr. John Wilkinson(Ph.D. class of 2022)Staff ScientistLawrence Livermore National LaboratoryRecent efforts studying the decay of 11Be highlight a potential new resonance between the proton and neutron separation energies of 11B. First noted by Riisager et al. 2014, surprisingly large yields of 10Be were observed in this narrow energy band. Follow on studies disagree on the existence or underlying properties of the resonance. An alternative approach studying the 7Li(a,p)10Be reaction will be presented. Offline analysis via 10Be accelerator mass spectrometry (AMS) is performed at CAMS. A broader facility overview and other nuclear data efforts will also be highlighted. This work was performed under the auspices of the U.S. Department of Energy by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory under contract DE-AC52 07NA27344 and supported by the LLNL-LDRD Program under Project No. 26-LW-028. Hosted by Dr. deBoer

events.title: Celebrating the Big Draw Festival: Make Your Mark
events.summary: In celebration of the international Big Draw Festival, drawing materials will be available to satisfy your creative itch all October long. Head to the Learning Commons to pick up supplies (or bring your own–solid graphite only, please) and then into the galleries to sketch one of your favorite works of art. Take your drawing with you or add it to the display wall to share with others. Parking is available in the Visitor Lot immediately north of the Sculpture Park for a fee during the week (before 4:30 p.m.). Free two-hour parking is available in the Eddy Street Commons Parking Garage or along Angela Blvd. After 4:30 p.m. and on weekends, parking is free and available in any non-gated campus lot. If traveling via South Bend Transpo, take the No.7 bus and use the Eddy St. Commons stop. About the Big Draw Festival The Big Draw Festival is a worldwide celebration of drawing, bringing people together through the power of creativity. The Festival provides a platform to explore drawing and mark-making in all its forms. Since its launch in 2000, The Big Draw has championed the universal language of drawing as a tool for learning, expression, and innovation. By taking part, you join a global movement that promotes creativity, wellbeing, and arts education. Originally published at raclinmurphymuseum.nd.edu.

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.summary: ND NEURO ROUNDS A Bi-Weekly Cutting-Edge Research Review Clinic DISCOVER THE SCIENCE. DECONSTRUCT THE DATA. MEET ND NEUROSCIENTISTS Join Notre Dame’s premier neuroscience research forum. ND Neuro Rounds brings together faculty, postdocs, graduate students, and undergraduates to collaboratively analyze the most groundbreaking, high-impact neuroscience publications in real time. Whether you are a seasoned investigator or an undergraduate looking to build foundational research skills, ND Neuro Rounds offers a unique seat at the scientific table. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: Fall Undergraduate Research Fair (FURF)
events.summary: The purpose of the Fall Undergraduate Research Fair (FURF) is to provide students an opportunity to have their questions answered about undergraduate research. Students can discover not only how to get involved in research, but also how to get more out of the research experience.Throughout and beyond the College of Science, there are many avenues for students to participate in research during their undergraduate years. Often it’s just a question of looking in the right places and being persistent in the hunt for the right opportunity. However, finding the right opportunity is also about gleaning as much information as possible from a diversityof sources. Through a combination of listening to speakers, poster presenters, and representatives from various institutions, students glean ideas about get started with research opportunities. Students will see how they can add value to their research experience by participating in related activities. The sooner they begin their search, the sooner they will start participating in undergraduate research and getting the most from that experience. Register to present your poster by Monday, October 5

events.title: Friday Pitches
events.summary: Have an idea? We want to hear about it! Aspiring entrepreneurs are invited to pitch their ideas every Friday to the IDEA Center and other investors. Each idea presented has the chance to earn up to $1,000.00! Pitches take place on Fridays from 12:30 pm - 3:00 pm in Room 160 at the IDEA Center (except during planned University closures or holidays). Each presentation consists of a 10-minute pitch, with asks for feedback, advice, and/or funding, followed by a 15-minute Q&A. Any student is welcome to attend and watch. To get started, submit your idea. A Startup Coach will then meet with you one-on-one to help you create a roadmap for fine-tuning your idea, gathering data, and building a presentation. When you are ready, your coach will help you sign up for a Pitch Fridays time slot. Originally published at ideacenter.nd.edu.

events.title: Open Studio
events.summary: Join in for Open Studio, a monthly drop-in program designed to help you connect with your creative side. This program encourages participants to engage with materials in guided or freestyle ways, inspired by the themes, techniques, and media of a featured work of art. This season, the focus will be on Signs and Configurations by Joan Miro. Each month, there will be a different project, allowing for new ways to connect with this work. The studio host will be available to guide you through the month’s project or support you in your creative endeavors. All materials are provided. Drop in when you can and stay as long as you like. Parking is available in the Visitor Lot immediately behind the museum, north of the Sculpture Park, for free after 4:30 p.m. and on weekends. Parking can also be found along Angela Blvd. If traveling via South Bend Transpo, take the No.7 bus and use the stop at Notre Dame Ave. and Angela Blvd. Originally published at raclinmurphymuseum.nd.edu.

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.

events.summary: The Notre Dame Scientific Artificial Intelligence (SAI) Initiative sponsors the SAI-Spark tutorial series. events.title: Nuclear Physics Seminar: Dr. David Neto, Michigan State University
events.summary: JINA-REACLIB Thermonuclear Reaction Database Dr. David NetoPostdoctoral FellowFacility for Rare Isotope BeamsMichigan State University Astrophysical models and simulations depend on a wide range of nuclear data: from masses, half-lives, levels, spins, and reaction rates. The JINA-REACLIB database, now a CeNAM project, is an ongoing effort to maintain a current, accurate, and publicly available library of thermonuclear reaction rates for astrophysical applications. In this talk, I will give a brief history of JINA-REACLIB before discussing the new workflow for collecting, reviewing, and evaluating nuclear physics data relevant for thermonuclear reaction rates. The current data pipeline and changes to increase the evaluation throughput and reduce the backlog of rates to be updated will be discussed. In addition to providing an overview of the progress of upcoming updates of several reaction rates. Finally, I will conclude with a preview of potential updates to the REACLIB database, including uncertainties, expanded format options, and highlight the need and opportunity for community input and feedback. Hosted by Dr. deBoer

events.title: Sacred Art "Visio Divina"
events.summary: Visio Divina, or “sacred seeing,” is an ancient form of Christian prayer in which we allow our hearts and imaginations to prayerfully and meditatively enter into an image. Join the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art for guided sessions of visio divina with sacred art in the Mary, Queen of Families Chapel. This opportunity is a wonderful way to spiritually engage with this unique, art-filled space. Whether you are new to the practice of visio divina or a long-time devotee, all are welcome for a moment of peace, prayer, and meditation. Meet at the Welcome Desk on Level 1. Always free and open to all. Originally published at raclinmurphymuseum.nd.edu.

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

Each Football Friday, join an exhibition tour of Mimmo Paladino: Present into Past to learn more about this contemporary artist and leading figure of the Italian avant-garde. Mimmo Paladino’s ambitious and bold oeuvre spans sacred art and liturgical objects, literary interpretations, and historical works. events.title: Notre Dame Seminars on Sustainability: Justin Farrell
events.summary: Join the Just Transformations to Sustainability Initiative in welcoming Professor Justin Farrell for the Notre Dame Seminars on Sustainability Series. We invite all attendees to stay afterward for lunch, conversation, and fellowship in 125 DeBartolo Hall as we work together to grow this vital network on campus. Justin Farrell is Professor of Sociology at the Yale School of the Environment. He studies how values, history, and environment shape communities. His books have been published by Princeton University Press, with a new book forthcoming from Norton, and his research articles have appeared in Science, PNAS, and the American Sociological Review, among others. His research has been supported by the Environmental Protection Agency and the National Science Foundation. He is an elected member of the Pontifical Academy of Social Sciences at the Vatican, and a proud Notre Dame graduate. More details to be announced soon. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.

events.title: SAI-Spark Tutorial Series
events.summary: The Notre Dame Scientific Artificial Intelligence (SAI) Initiative sponsors the SAI-Spark tutorial series. These comprise weekly standalone tutorials designed to illuminate the rapidly evolving interface between AI and scientific research. Sparks are open to graduate students, postdocs, and faculty across all disciplines. These hands-on sessions provide practical, immediately applicable knowledge in cutting-edge AI techniques. Each week features a different AI topic, allowing participants to explore AI applications without requiring semester-long commitment. Whether you’re new to AI, interested in networking with the SAI community on campus, or just looking to expand your toolkit on a few topics, SAI-Sparks offers accessible entry points to the interface of AI and scientific research. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: Algebraic Geometry and Commutative Algebra Seminar: Manav Batavia - Purdue University
events.summary: Speaker: Manav BataviaPurdue UniversityWill give a Algebraic Geometry and Commutative Algebra Seminar entitled:A sharp upper bound on cohomological dimension in unramified mixed characteristicAbstract: Given an ideal I in a regular local ring A, the cohomological dimension of I in A is the index of the highest non-vanishing local cohomology of A supported at I. Determining effective upper bounds on the cohomological dimension in terms of topological invariants of Spec(A/I) is a central problem in commutative algebra: foundational results include the Hartshorne--Lichtenbaum Vanishing Theorem and the Second Vanishing Theorem. In equal characteristic, Faltings established in 1980 a general bound on the cohomological dimension of an ideal in terms of its “big height”. In this talk, we extend Faltings’ results to the unramified mixed characteristic setting and show that the resulting bound is sharp.Date: 11-12-2026Time: 3:30 pmLocation: 258 Hurley Hall Download Poster [PDF, 235k]

events.title: Mimmo Paladino: Present into Past Exhibition Tour
events.summary: Mimmo Paladino, Untitled, 2019, Mixed media. On loan, Courtesy of the artist, to the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art, University of Notre Dame, IL2026.004.004. © Mimmo Paladino, All rights reserved. Each Football Friday, join an exhibition tour of Mimmo Paladino: Present into Past to learn more about this contemporary artist and leading figure of the Italian avant-garde. events.title: Friday Pitches
events.summary: Have an idea? We want to hear about it! Aspiring entrepreneurs are invited to pitch their ideas every Friday to the IDEA Center and other investors. Each idea presented has the chance to earn up to $1,000.00! Pitches take place on Fridays from 12:30 pm - 3:00 pm in Room 160 at the IDEA Center (except during planned University closures or holidays). Each presentation consists of a 10-minute pitch, with asks for feedback, advice, and/or funding, followed by a 15-minute Q&A. Any student is welcome to attend and watch. To get started, submit your idea. A Startup Coach will then meet with you one-on-one to help you create a roadmap for fine-tuning your idea, gathering data, and building a presentation. When you are ready, your coach will help you sign up for a Pitch Fridays time slot. Originally published at ideacenter.nd.edu.
