events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.

events.title: SAI-Spark Tutorial Series
events.summary: The Notre Dame Scientific Artificial Intelligence (SAI) Initiative sponsors the SAI-Spark tutorial series. These comprise weekly standalone tutorials designed to illuminate the rapidly evolving interface between AI and scientific research. Sparks are open to graduate students, postdocs, and faculty across all disciplines. These hands-on sessions provide practical, immediately applicable knowledge in cutting-edge AI techniques. Each week features a different AI topic, allowing participants to explore AI applications without requiring semester-long commitment. Whether you’re new to AI, interested in networking with the SAI community on campus, or just looking to expand your toolkit on a few topics, SAI-Sparks offers accessible entry points to the interface of AI and scientific research. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.

events.title: Korea Working Group Public Lecture — "Against Abandonment: Repertoires of Solidarity in South Korean Protest"
events.summary: Against Abandonment: Repertoires of Solidarity in South Korean Protest (Stanford University Press, 2025) offers insight into the utility and futility of protesting precarity under neoliberal capitalism. Based on long-term ethnographic research and in-depth interviews with key labor and social movement activists, the book follows the protests of minoritized workers, especially women employed in precarious jobs, as they contend with what it means to be treated as disposable and what it takes to resist. Long-term protest camps, life-threatening hunger strikes, grueling prostrations, perilous high-altitude occupations are agonizing to perform and to witness, but often powerful as effective catalysts of change. Through dramatic performances and rituals that repeat across time and space, Against Abandonment finds that protesters cultivate repertoires of solidarity as a relational force that binds people and worlds together in a collective praxis of refusal. In doing so, Against Abandonment builds upon intersectional, transnational, and abolitionist feminist theorizing that has long emphasized the centrality of building relations of care and community in place-based struggles against capitalist abandonment. Jennifer Jihye Chun is professor of Asian American Studies and Labor Studies and chair of the UCLA Labor Studies Department. She is associate director of the Institute for Research on Labor and Employment (IRLE), where she leads the Transnational Gender and Labor Working Group, a joint initiative between the IRLE and the Center for the Study of Women (CSW)|Streisand Center. Her research and teaching focus on the interconnected worlds of labor, gender, race, migration, and social movements under global capitalism. This lecture is sponsored by the Liu Institute's Korea Working Group, Gender Studies Program, Higgins Labor Program, and Department of Sociology. Originally published at asia.nd.edu.

Each tour explores a distinct source of artistic inspiration by pairing works from the temporary exhibition with works from the Museum’s permanent collection. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.

events.title: Notre Dame Seminars on Sustainability: Benjamin Sovacool - Conceptual frameworks and new frontiers in energy justice
events.summary: Join the Just Transformations to Sustainability Initiative in welcoming Professor Benjamin Sovacool for the Notre Dame Seminars on Sustainability Series. We invite all attendees to stay afterward for lunch, conversation, and fellowship in 125 DeBartolo Hall as we work together to grow this vital network on campus. Benjamin K. Sovacool is Professor of Earth and Environment at Boston University in the United States, where he is the Founding Director of the Institute for Global Sustainability. He is also Professor of Energy Policy at the Bennett Institute for Innovation & Policy Acceleration at the University of Sussex Business School. He is a Fellow of the Royal Society for Arts, Manufactures and Commerce, a Fellow of the Academy of Social Sciences, and a Fellow in the Academy of Europe (Academia Europaea). This presentation explores how concepts from justice and ethics can inform energy decision-making and highlight the futurity, fairness, and equity dimensions of energy production and use. It defines "energy justice" as a global energy system that fairly distributes both the benefits […] look at the Rights of Nature or non-anthropocentric notions of justice. Third is focusing on cross-scalar issues of justice such as embodied emissions. Fourth is identifying business models and the co-benefits of justice. Fifth is better understanding the tradeoffs within energy justice principles. Sixth is confronting utopian or falsely constructed justice discourses. In doing so, the presentation argues in favor of "justice-aware" energy planning and policymaking, and it hopes that its (reconsidered) energy justice conceptual framework offers a critical tool to inform decision-making. Originally published at sustainabilityinitiative.nd.edu. This is an excerpt of a longer announcement. Consult the original listing for full program, registration, and attendance requirements.

events.title: Film: Mimmo Paladino's Quijote (2006)
events.summary: Quijote (2006)Director: Mimmo PaladinoRuntime: 75 minutesLanguages: Italian with English subtitlesProduction: Italy | Ananas A visionary journey into the world of Cervantes’ antihero, where the wandering knight traverses ancient and contemporary landscapes inhabited by symbols, apparitions, and timeless figures. Mimmo Paladino transforms Don Quixote into a cinematic tapestry of images in which painting, theatre, music, and film merge into a procession of poets, magicians, emperors, and madmen. Suspended between myth and dream, and accompanied by the music of Lucio Dalla, Quijote restores to its wandering knight the inexhaustible power of utopia. This film is being screened as part of the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art’s temporary exhibition Mimmo Paladino: Present into Past. The screening will be followed by a conversation with Joseph Becherer, exhibition curator and director of the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art, and Juan Vitulli, associate professor of Spanish. This is a free but ticketed event. Visit the DeBartolo Performing Art Center's website to reserve your ticket. Co-sponsored by the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art and the Browning Cinema at the DeBartolo Performing Arts Center. Originally published at raclinmurphymuseum.nd.edu.

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: SAI-Spark Tutorial Series
events.summary: The Notre Dame Scientific Artificial Intelligence (SAI) Initiative sponsors the SAI-Spark tutorial series. These comprise weekly standalone tutorials designed to illuminate the rapidly evolving interface between AI and scientific research. Sparks are open to graduate students, postdocs, and faculty across all disciplines. These hands-on sessions provide practical, immediately applicable knowledge in cutting-edge AI techniques. Each week features a different AI topic, allowing participants to explore AI applications without requiring semester-long commitment. Whether you’re new to AI, interested in networking with the SAI community on campus, or just looking to expand your toolkit on a few topics, SAI-Sparks offers accessible entry points to the interface of AI and scientific research. For additional information please visit our SAI-Sparks page. Originally published at sai.nd.edu.

MEET ND NEUROSCIENTISTS Join Notre Dame’s premier neuroscience research forum. ND Neuro Rounds brings together faculty, postdocs, graduate students, and undergraduates to collaboratively analyze the most groundbreaking, high-impact neuroscience publications in real time. Whether you are a seasoned investigator or an undergraduate looking to build foundational research skills, ND Neuro Rounds offers a unique seat at the scientific table. events.title: Friday Pitches
events.summary: Have an idea? We want to hear about it! Aspiring entrepreneurs are invited to pitch their ideas every Friday to the IDEA Center and other investors. Each idea presented has the chance to earn up to $1,000.00! Pitches take place on Fridays from 12:30 pm - 3:00 pm in Room 160 at the IDEA Center (except during planned University closures or holidays). Each presentation consists of a 10-minute pitch, with asks for feedback, advice, and/or funding, followed by a 15-minute Q&A. Any student is welcome to attend and watch. To get started, submit your idea. A Startup Coach will then meet with you one-on-one to help you create a roadmap for fine-tuning your idea, gathering data, and building a presentation. When you are ready, your coach will help you sign up for a Pitch Fridays time slot. Originally published at ideacenter.nd.edu.

events.title: SAI-Spark Tutorial Series
events.summary: The Notre Dame Scientific Artificial Intelligence (SAI) Initiative sponsors the SAI-Spark tutorial series. These comprise weekly standalone tutorials designed to illuminate the rapidly evolving interface between AI and scientific research. Sparks are open to graduate students, postdocs, and faculty across all disciplines. These hands-on sessions provide practical, immediately applicable knowledge in cutting-edge AI techniques. Each week features a different AI topic, allowing participants to explore AI applications without requiring semester-long commitment. Whether you’re new to AI, interested in networking with the SAI community on campus, or just looking to expand your toolkit on a few topics, SAI-Sparks offers accessible entry points to the interface of AI and scientific research. For additional information please visit our SAI-Sparks page. Originally published at sai.nd.edu.

events.title: Nuclear Physics Seminar: Dr. Sabrina Strauss, Viridien
events.summary: Journey to Atlantis: Transitioning from Nuclear Physics to Geophysics Dr. Sabrina Strauss(PhD class of 2020)Imaging Project CoordinatorViridien When journeying into industry, away from the well-beaten path of academia, one major hurdle is translating your academic skills into skills marketable to new sectors. Dr. Sabrina Strauss will discuss her transition from nuclear physics research to geophysics and seismic imaging at Viridien. She explores how the research skills learned for nuclear physics translate to tasks handled in projects every day at Viridien. Through the lens of the Atlantis oil field, we discover the insights gained not only into the oil field, but also the boundaries advanced and pushed for the industry as a whole. Hosted by Prof. Aprahamian

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.summary: Visio Divina, or “sacred seeing,” is an ancient form of Christian prayer in which we allow our hearts and imaginations to prayerfully and meditatively enter into an image. Join the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art for guided sessions of visio divina with sacred art in the Mary, Queen of Families Chapel. This opportunity is a wonderful way to spiritually engage with this unique, art-filled space. Whether you are new to the practice of visio divina or a long-time devotee, all are welcome for a moment of peace, prayer, and meditation. Meet at the Welcome Desk on Level 1. Always free and open to all. Originally published at raclinmurphymuseum.nd.edu.

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.

events.title: Notre Dame Seminars on Sustainability: Elena Bennett - Measuring what Matters: A social-ecological systems ecologist’s perspective
events.summary: Join the Just Transformations to Sustainability Initiative in welcoming Professor Elena Bennett for the Notre Dame Seminars on Sustainability Series. We invite all attendees to stay afterward for lunch, conversation, and fellowship in 125 DeBartolo Hall as we work together to grow this vital network on campus. Elena Bennett is Professor and Canada Research Chair in Sustainability Science at McGill University. Her work focuses on the interactions among ecosystem services and how we can manage these interactions for multifunctional working landscapes, using a landscape ecology and systems ecology perspective. She is the Director of ResNet, a 100+ person NSERC Strategic Network that works with communities in six working landscapes across Canada to address questions about managing ecosystem service provision. More details to be announced soon. Originally published at sustainabilityinitiative.nd.edu.

events.title: Friday Pitches
events.summary: Have an idea? We want to hear about it! Aspiring entrepreneurs are invited to pitch their ideas every Friday to the IDEA Center and other investors. Each idea presented has the chance to earn up to $1,000.00! Pitches take place on Fridays from 12:30 pm - 3:00 pm in Room 160 at the IDEA Center (except during planned University closures or holidays). Each presentation consists of a 10-minute pitch, with asks for feedback, advice, and/or funding, followed by a 15-minute Q&A. Any student is welcome to attend and watch. To get started, submit your idea. A Startup Coach will then meet with you one-on-one to help you create a roadmap for fine-tuning your idea, gathering data, and building a presentation. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

Tap your toes to live holiday music from the Music Village Jammers—and feel free to pick up an instrument and join the fun! Warm up with cocoa and cookies provided by the Friends of the Raclin Murphy Museum. Make warm winter memories at the Raclin Murphy Museum with friends, family, and neighbors. Parking is available in the Visitor Lot immediately behind the Museum, north of the Sculpture Park, for free after 4:30 p.m. and on weekends. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

We invite all attendees to stay afterward for lunch, conversation, and fellowship in 125 DeBartolo Hall as we work together to grow this vital network on campus. Maximilian Auffhammer is the George Pardee Jr. Professor of International Sustainable Development and Chair of the Berkeley Division of the Academic Senate. More details to be announced soon. Originally published at sustainabilityinitiative.nd.edu.
events.hostOrganization: College of Science

events.title: Friday Pitches
events.summary: Have an idea? We want to hear about it! Aspiring entrepreneurs are invited to pitch their ideas every Friday to the IDEA Center and other investors. Each idea presented has the chance to earn up to $1,000.00! Pitches take place on Fridays from 12:30 pm - 3:00 pm in Room 160 at the IDEA Center (except during planned University closures or holidays). Each presentation consists of a 10-minute pitch, with asks for feedback, advice, and/or funding, followed by a 15-minute Q&A. Any student is welcome to attend and watch. To get started, submit your idea. A Startup Coach will then meet with you one-on-one to help you create a roadmap for fine-tuning your idea, gathering data, and building a presentation. When you are ready, your coach will help you sign up for a Pitch Fridays time slot. Originally published at ideacenter.nd.edu.

events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: Artful Storytime
events.summary: Designed to help children develop their visual and verbal literacy skills, Artful Storytime is a partnership with the St. Joseph County Public Library. Each Artful Storytime includes stories, songs, artwork explorations, art-making, and more. This month, we’re slowing down and exercising our observation skills. Come ready to discover tiny details and explore BIG ideas! This program is best for families with children ages 4 to 6. Parking is available in the Visitor Lot immediately behind the museum, north of the Sculpture Park, for free after 4:30 p.m. and on weekends. Parking can also be found along Angela Blvd. If traveling via South Bend Transpo, take the No.7 bus and use the stop at Notre Dame Ave. and Angela Blvd. Originally published at raclinmurphymuseum.nd.edu.

events.title: The Met Opera Live in HD: "The Magic Flute" (Mozart)
events.summary: The Met Opera Live in HD120 minutes (No intermission) EncoreA favorite holiday tradition, the Met's abridged, English-language version of Julie Taymor's whimsical production returns with conductor James Levine. Tenor Matthew Polenzani stars in the role of Tamino and Pamina is sung by soprano Ying Huang. The cast also features baritone Nathan Gunn as Papageno, soprano Erika Miklósa as the Queen of the Night, and bass René Pape as Sarastro. GET TICKETS *Sponsored by the Jill A. Fischer Endowment for Excellence in Live Opera Broadcasts.
events.location: Browning Cinema, DeBartolo Performing Arts Center

events.summary: The CRC offers multiple training opportunities for both new and existing users. We periodically provide short courses and other learning opportunities, which are advertised on our website and through email list. In-person office hours are held every Wednesday and Thursday from 2:00-3:30 pm in Flanner Hall, room 812, on a first-come, first-served basis. events.title: Photographic Exhibit — "Mantelpieces and the Mundane: Homemaking and Ireland’s Disappearing History"
events.summary: Drawing on 18 years of photographic research on the island of Inishbofin, Ireland, Professor Ian Kuijt (Department of Anthropology, Notre Dame) explores mantelpieces, homemaking, and Ireland’s disappearing history in this photographic exhibit. Based on single-frame color photographic images as well as large-scale composite panoramas comprising 30–40 images, the photographs in this exhibit focus on the central room of post-1900 buildings. The images explore how the mantelpiece served as a location of display above the central hearth and consider the material world of what was left behind on the mantelpiece and in the home when Islanders moved away. This creative research produces large-scale photographs to reflect upon the soft footprint of intergenerational rural abandonment. Open to the public during Hesburgh Library operating hours. About the Artist Ian Kuijt is a professor of anthropology at the University of Notre Dame. As an archaeologist, film-maker, and photographer, he conducts multidisciplinary research that combines anthropology with historical and prehistoric archaeology. He is the author of Island Places, Island Lives: Exploring Inishbofin and Inishark Heritage, Co. Galway, Ireland. Wordwell, Ltd, Dublin, co-editor of The Archaeology of Ireland in the Age of Improvement, Routledge Press, and the 2026 social documentary film 14 Liters of Ukrainian Blood (14 літрів української крові) (75 min), which explores the human impact of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. He is the director of the Cultural Landscapes of the Irish Coast Project.
events.location: Hesburgh Library, 2nd Floor, outside the Holtz Grand Reading Room

events.title: CRC New User Training
events.summary: The CRC offers multiple training opportunities for both new and existing users. We periodically provide short courses and other learning opportunities, which are advertised on our website and through email list. In-person office hours are held every Wednesday and Thursday from 2:00-3:30 pm in Flanner Hall, room 812, on a first-come, first-served basis. You can also arrange a Zoom meeting at your convenience by emailing CRCSupport@nd.edu with your availability. We recommend bringing a laptop to in-person sessions. A CRC User Account is required to participate. If you need an account, please fill out and submit the CRC Account Request Form. Office hours will be held in 812 Flanner Hall. Click here to register. For more information, please contact CRCsupport@nd.edu. Originally published at crc.nd.edu.
